picks.file: Adana, Mount Taurus in the distance - Carne John - 1836.jpg
picks.what: The town on the river with the Taurus Mountains beyond, steel engraving in John Carne’s Syria, the Holy Land, Asia Minor
picks.why: true general view: castle and minarets above the Seyhan with the Taurus range behind; engraved caption cut off

picks.what: Houses along the Seyhan River, colored postcard
picks.why: labeled Adana, river quarter: old houses lining the river wall; postcard margin and caption cut off

gaps: P0–P2: nothing; P6: only gray, hazy views from a shopping mall (#11, #12), a park in the museum grounds and the castle of Yılankale outside the city, skipped
notes: #1’s artist line is too small to read in the copy (the series was drawn by W. H. Bartlett, William Purser and others); the Commons date is 1836, the series ran 1836–38. #8’s date (4 January 1921) comes from the Houshamadyan record and is probably when the card was written or mailed, so the photograph may be a few years older; labeled “about 1920”. #11 (2016) shows the snow-capped Taurus and a tower the file calls the clock tower, but it is gray and hazy with billboards in front; the reviewer could use it for P6 trimmed to [0, 0.22, 0.9, 0.66] if a weak modern view is preferred to a blank plate. #4 (General Gouraud’s arrival, 1920) is a station scene with troops, skipped.
